title: Visual Assessment of Echocardiography and Arterial Waveforms for Intraoperative Fluid Management: Validation Against Hemodynamic Reference Parameters
summary:
This study investigates how confidently doctors can decide whether patients need additional fluids (e.g. infusions) or not. In everyday clinical practice, such decisions are often based on experience - for example, by assessing the blood pressure curve, the configuration of the pulse pressure curve and/or additional ultrasound images of the heart.

The study uses real measurement data from patients after an operation, in which arterial blood pressure was recorded simultaneously via a catheter, values from extended haemodynamic monitoring and ultrasound images of the heart (four-chamber view) and the inferior vena cava. Doctors assess these data sets and decide on this basis whether they would initiate fluid therapy at this point in time. They are not shown the values from the extended haemodynamic monitoring.

This situation is very practical, as advanced haemodynamic monitors are not available everywhere and their use is often limited - especially due to expensive disposable items. The aim of the study is to find out whether clinical decisions can be made reliably without these specialised devices - or whether their use offers measurable added value for patient care.
